# Alluvial charts {#sec-alluvial-charts}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_y2k(
    base_size = 13))
# pak::pak("corybrunson/ggalluvial")
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_y2k()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_y2k()`, built from the Y2K countdown: a black terminal background, a red LED frame and title, red, amber, green, silver, and blue screen marks, and a PT Mono title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggalluvial)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
prep_levels <- c("Not worried", "Some supplies", "Bunker ready")
move_probs <- matrix(c(0.70, 0.25, 0.05,
                       0.15, 0.65, 0.20,
                       0.05, 0.15, 0.80),
                     nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
                     dimnames = list(prep_levels, prep_levels))
next_survey <- function(prep) {
  vapply(prep, function(p) {
    sample(prep_levels, size = 1, prob = move_probs[p, ])
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
set.seed(1999)
y2k_households <- tibble(
  household_id = 1:300,
  jan_1999 = sample(prep_levels, size = 300, replace = TRUE,
                    prob = c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1))) |>
  mutate(jul_1999 = next_survey(jan_1999),
         dec_1999 = next_survey(jul_1999)) |>
  mutate(across(-household_id, function(x) factor(x, levels = prep_levels)))
y2k_wide <- y2k_households |>
  count(jan_1999, jul_1999, dec_1999, name = "freq")
labs_alluvial <- labs(title = "Y2K prep",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "300 households surveyed three times in 1999")
labs_alluvial_y <- ylab("Households")

ggp2_alluvial_w <- ggplot(data = y2k_wide,
  aes(axis1 = jan_1999, axis2 = jul_1999,
      axis3 = dec_1999, y = freq)) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Jan 1999", "Jul 1999", "Dec 1999"),
    expand = c(0.1, 0.07)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = jan_1999)) +
  geom_stratum() +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum",
    aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),
      size = 3)

ggp2_alluvial_w +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs_alluvial +
  labs_alluvial_y
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ multiple categorical variables**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a date or time variable**
:::

::::

## Description

An alluvial chart shows how the parts of a whole change,[^composition] or how things move from group to group, over time or from one way of sorting them to the next.[^categories]

We can make alluvial charts in `ggplot2` with code from [`ggalluvial`](https://corybrunson.github.io/ggalluvial/).[^ggalluvial]

See also: [parallel sets](parallel_sets.qmd)

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages]


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
# pak::pak("corybrunson/ggalluvial")
library(ggalluvial)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for data manipulation
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

Y2K is a short way to say the year 2000, and January, July, and December are months of the year. As 1999 went on, the news was full of talk about the Y2K problem:[^y2k-bug] computers that kept only the last two numbers of each year[^digits] could think January 1, 2000 was January 1, 1900, and nobody was quite sure what would break. We'll make up[^simulate] 300 homes[^households] and ask each one three times in 1999 (January, July, and December) how ready they were:[^surveyed] `"Not worried"`, `"Some supplies"` (extra water and other things they could need),[^supplies] or `"Bunker ready"`. A bunker is a strong room under the ground where people go to be safe.

In January, more than half of the homes are `"Not worried"` (we pick these with `sample()`). After that, each home's next answer turns only on its last answer. The `move_probs` table[^matrix] holds those chances: each row is where a home is now, and each column is where it could be the next time we ask. For example, a home that is `"Not worried"` has a 70% chance of staying that way, a 25% chance of moving to `"Some supplies"`, and a 5% chance of going all the way to `"Bunker ready"`. `next_survey()` uses `sample()` to pick each home's next answer from its row. Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same 300 homes every time you run the code below.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
prep_levels <- c("Not worried", "Some supplies", "Bunker ready") # three levels of Y2K preparation
move_probs <- matrix(
  c(0.70, 0.25, 0.05, # from 'Not worried'
    0.15, 0.65, 0.20, # from 'Some supplies'
    0.05, 0.15, 0.80), # from 'Bunker ready'
  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE, # rows are where a household starts
  dimnames = list(prep_levels, prep_levels) # columns are where it ends up
  )
next_survey <- function(prep) { # moves each household to its next level
  vapply(prep, function(p) {
    sample(prep_levels, size = 1, prob = move_probs[p, ]) # use the row for its current level
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
set.seed(1999) # same 300 households every time the code runs
y2k_households <- tibble(
  household_id = 1:300, # 300 different households, one row each
  jan_1999 = sample(prep_levels,
    size = 300, # one starting level for each household
    replace = TRUE, # levels repeat across households
    prob = c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1) # most households start out 'Not worried'
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    jul_1999 = next_survey(jan_1999), # second survey builds on the first
    dec_1999 = next_survey(jul_1999) # third survey builds on the second
    ) |>
  mutate(
    across(-household_id, function(x) factor(x, levels = prep_levels)) # keep the level order
    )
glimpse(y2k_households)
```
:::

Below we find how many homes gave each set of three answers (as `y2k_wide`).[^combination] Each row is one way through the three times we ask, and `freq` is how many homes went that way.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_y2k_wide
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
y2k_wide <- y2k_households |>
  count(jan_1999, jul_1999, dec_1999, # every path through the three surveys
    name = "freq" # number of households on each path
    )
glimpse(y2k_wide)
```
:::

## Distribution

An alluvial chart shows how things move from group to group. How wide each band is[^flow] tells us how many homes it holds, and those numbers come from a line of moves made by chance:[^chain] each home leaves its next answer up to chance every time we ask. Below we'll move from the homes, to a graph, to the rule behind it.[^formula]

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first five homes.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(y2k_households, 5)
```
:::

Some homes stay put and some move. Below we set January's answers (rows) against July's answers (columns) with `table()`.[^crosstab]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
jan_jul <- table(January = y2k_households$jan_1999,
                 July = y2k_households$jul_1999)
jan_jul
```
:::

Of the `r sum(jan_jul["Not worried", ])` homes that were `"Not worried"` in January, `r jan_jul["Not worried", "Not worried"]` were still `"Not worried"` in July. That's about `r round(100 * jan_jul["Not worried", "Not worried"] / sum(jan_jul["Not worried", ]))`%, close to the 70% in the first row of `move_probs`.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The alluvial chart below shows the same table. Each box[^cells] in `jan_jul` that is not 0 becomes a band from January to July, and how wide the band is shows the number in that box. That's `r sum(jan_jul > 0)` of the 9 boxes, because no home went from `"Bunker ready"` to `"Not worried"`.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
y2k_households |>
  count(jan_1999, jul_1999, name = "freq") |>
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = jan_1999, axis2 = jul_1999, y = freq)) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Jan 1999", "Jul 1999"),
                   expand = c(0.1, 0.07)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = jan_1999)) +
  geom_stratum() +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 3) +
  labs(y = "Households") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

The big numbers that run from the top left to the lower right of `move_probs`[^diagonal] make staying in the same group the most likely move, but how wide a band is also turns on how many homes start in that group. That's why the band from `"Not worried"` to `"Some supplies"` (`r jan_jul["Not worried", "Some supplies"]` homes) is wider than the band of homes that stay `"Bunker ready"` (`r jan_jul["Bunker ready", "Bunker ready"]` homes).

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

When each next step turns only on the step we're on now, we have [a line of steps that forgets the past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_chain).[^markov] The homes that start in each group break up across the three groups by [a rule for how many land in each group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinomial_distribution)[^multinomial] (the same rule we used for the last Alleyway stage each player reached in @sec-bar-graphs), with the chances from that group's row of `move_probs`:

$$
(N_{\text{not}}, N_{\text{some}}, N_{\text{bunker}}) \mid \text{Not worried} \sim \text{Multinomial}\left(n_{\text{not}}, \; (0.70, 0.25, 0.05)\right)
$$

Putting January's numbers through the table[^matrix-mult] gives the numbers we'd expect in July:

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: name_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
expected_jul <- as.vector(table(y2k_households$jan_1999)) %*% move_probs
rbind(expected = round(expected_jul[1, ], 1),
      observed = table(y2k_households$jul_1999))
```
:::

The July numbers we got land close to the ones we expected.[^observed] Because the chances of moving closer to the bunker (0.25 and 0.20) are bigger than the chances of moving back (0.15 and 0.15),[^off-diagonal] each new answer moves more homes over to the right side of the table. Try changing the first row of `move_probs` to `c(0.95, 0.04, 0.01)` and far more homes stay in the same group.

## Grammar

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::



  - Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()` and `ylab()`

  - Add `scale_x_discrete()` with `limits` set to `"Jan 1999"`, `"Jul 1999"` and `"Dec 1999"` (the names under the three axes), and `expand` set to `0.1` and `0.07` (room on each side)[^scale-x]

  - Add `geom_alluvium()` and give each `jan_1999` group its own color with `fill`, then add `geom_stratum()`[^stratum]

  - Add `geom_text()`, with `stat` set to `stratum` and `label` set to `after_stat(stratum)` (*inside* `aes()`), to write the name of each group on its box

  - Take away the key[^legend] with `theme(legend.position = "none")`, because the words on the boxes already name each group

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_alluvial
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_alluvial <- labs(title = "Y2K prep",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "300 households surveyed three times in 1999")
labs_alluvial_y <- ylab("Households")

ggp2_alluvial_w <- ggplot(data = y2k_wide,
  aes(axis1 = jan_1999, axis2 = jul_1999,
      axis3 = dec_1999, y = freq)) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Jan 1999", "Jul 1999", "Dec 1999"),
    expand = c(0.1, 0.07)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = jan_1999)) +
  geom_stratum() +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum",
    aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),
      size = 3)

ggp2_alluvial_w +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs_alluvial +
  labs_alluvial_y
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

The code in `ggalluvial` can work with wide or long data.[^wide-long]

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_alluvial
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_alluvial <- labs(title = "Y2K prep",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "300 households surveyed three times in 1999")
labs_alluvial_y <- ylab("Households")

ggp2_alluvial_w <- ggplot(data = y2k_wide,
  aes(axis1 = jan_1999, axis2 = jul_1999,
      axis3 = dec_1999, y = freq)) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Jan 1999", "Jul 1999", "Dec 1999"),
    expand = c(0.1, 0.07)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = jan_1999)) +
  geom_stratum() +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum",
    aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),
      size = 3)

ggp2_alluvial_w +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs_alluvial +
  labs_alluvial_y
```

## More info

`ggalluvial` can also help change the form of the data with `to_lodes_form()`.[^reshape]

### `to_lodes_form()`

Below we make `y2k_lodes` from the `y2k_wide` data with `to_lodes_form()` from `ggalluvial`. We'll also keep each home's January answer in a new column (`January`) so we can still use it for `fill` after we change the form of the data.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_y2k_lodes
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
y2k_lodes <- y2k_wide |>
  rename(`Jan 1999` = jan_1999, `Jul 1999` = jul_1999, # readable axis labels
         `Dec 1999` = dec_1999, Households = freq) |>
  mutate(January = `Jan 1999`) |> # keep each household's starting level for fill
  ggalluvial::to_lodes_form(
    key = "Survey", # new column holding the survey names
    axes = 1:3 # the three survey columns become the axes
    )
glimpse(y2k_lodes)
```
:::

Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()`

  - Put `Survey` on `x` and `Households` on `y`, and join `stratum` to `stratum`, `alluvium` to `alluvium`, and `label` to `stratum`.[^map]

  - Add `geom_alluvium()` and give each `January` group its own color with `fill`

  - Add `geom_stratum()` and set `width` to `0.45`

  - Add `geom_text()`, set `stat` to `"stratum"`, and set `size` to `3.5`

  - Take away the key with `theme(legend.position = "none")`, because the words on the boxes already name each group

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_alluvial_lf
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
labs_alluvial <- labs(title = "Y2K prep",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "300 households surveyed three times in 1999")

ggp2_alluvial_lf <- ggplot(
    data = y2k_lodes,
    aes(x = Survey,
        y = Households,
        stratum = stratum,
        alluvium = alluvium,
        label = stratum)) +
    ggalluvial::geom_alluvium(aes(fill = January)) +
    ggalluvial::geom_stratum(width = 0.45) +
    geom_text(stat = "stratum", size = 3.5)

ggp2_alluvial_lf +
    labs_alluvial +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

### `geom_flow()`

If you'd like to put the times[^date-var] across `x`, you can use `ggalluvial::geom_flow()` with `ggalluvial::geom_stratum()`.

  - First make `y2k_long`, a long form of `y2k_households` with one row for each home each time we ask (and `survey` set in the order we asked).[^factor]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_y2k_long
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
y2k_long <- y2k_households |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -household_id, # stack the three survey columns
    names_to = "survey", # which survey each row comes from
    values_to = "prep" # the household's level in that survey
    ) |>
  mutate(
    survey = factor(survey,
      levels = c("jan_1999", "jul_1999", "dec_1999"), # surveys in time order
      labels = c("Jan 1999", "Jul 1999", "Dec 1999") # readable labels
      ),
    household_id = factor(household_id) # each household is a category
    )
glimpse(y2k_long)
```
:::

  - Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()`

  - Start the graph with `ggplot()` and give it `data`

  - Put `survey` on `x`, and join `prep` to `stratum`, `household_id` to `alluvium`, `prep` to `fill`, and `prep` to `label`.[^map]

  - Add `geom_flow()`, with `stat` set to `"alluvium"` and `lode.guidance` set to `"frontback"` (with 300 homes, each band is only one home wide, so we leave the outside line `color` off, or it covers the `fill`)

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_alluvial_flow
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
# labels
labs_alluvial <- labs(
  title = "Y2K prep across three surveys",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "Survey", y = "Households",
  fill = "Prep")
# add geom_flow()
ggp2_alluvial_flow <- ggplot(data = y2k_long,
  mapping = aes(x = survey, stratum = prep,
    alluvium = household_id,
    fill = prep, label = prep)) +
  geom_flow(stat = "alluvium",
    lode.guidance = "frontback")

ggp2_alluvial_flow +
  labs_alluvial
```
:::

  - Add `ggalluvial::geom_stratum()`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_alluvial_stratum
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
# add geom_stratum()
ggp2_alluvial_stratum <- ggp2_alluvial_flow +
  geom_stratum()
ggp2_alluvial_stratum +
  labs_alluvial
```
:::

### `legend.position`

Move the key[^legend] under the graph with `theme(legend.position = "bottom")`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_alluvial_legend
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggp2_alluvial_stratum +
  labs_alluvial +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

[^composition]: Changes in composition.

[^categories]: Flow over time or across multiple categorical variables.

[^ggalluvial]: The `ggalluvial` package.

[^packages]: Install and load the packages.

[^y2k-bug]: The Y2K bug (also called the millennium bug).

[^digits]: Stored years with two digits (`99` for 1999).

[^simulate]: Simulate.

[^households]: Households.

[^surveyed]: Surveyed three times about how prepared they were.

[^supplies]: Extra batteries and bottled water.

[^matrix]: The `move_probs` matrix of transition probabilities.

[^seed]: Setting the random seed.

[^combination]: Count every combination of the three answers.

[^flow]: The width of each flow (alluvium).

[^chain]: A chain of random moves (a Markov chain).

[^formula]: The formula.

[^crosstab]: A cross tabulation (contingency table).

[^cells]: Cells.

[^diagonal]: The diagonal of the matrix.

[^markov]: A Markov chain.

[^multinomial]: A multinomial distribution: the counts in each of $k$ categories across $n$ independent trials with fixed probabilities.

[^matrix-mult]: Multiplying January's counts by the matrix (matrix multiplication with `%*%`).

[^observed]: The observed July counts land close to the expected counts.

[^off-diagonal]: The off diagonal probabilities.

[^labels]: Labels.

[^scale-x]: A discrete `x` scale with one limit for each axis and expansion on both sides.

[^stratum]: Each stratum is a box for one category at one axis.

[^wide-long]: Wide data has one column for each axis (`y2k_wide`); long (lodes) data has one row for each path at each axis (`y2k_lodes`).

[^reshape]: Reshape the data from wide (alluvia) form to long (lodes) form.

[^map]: Map these variables inside `aes()`.

[^date-var]: The date or time variable.

[^factor]: `survey` is a factor with its levels in time order.

[^legend]: The legend.
